item.text: The file contains 90 measurements: three specimens per material, each measured over the same strain range. The curves look linear across the supplied range, so I’ll fit one pooled stress–strain line per material and show the individual specimen readings alongside those fits.

# Tensile test results

Elastic modulus was estimated as the slope of an ordinary least-squares linear fit of stress (MPa) against strain for each material. The fit pooled all 30 measurements from its three specimens, used the full supplied strain range (0.0002–0.0020), and included a fitted intercept.

| Material | Measurements | Elastic modulus (GPa) | R² |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Aluminum | 30 | 69.38 | 0.99834 |
| Steel | 30 | 199.06 | 0.99844 |
| Titanium | 30 | 116.56 | 0.99788 |

All three datasets are strongly linear over the measured range (R² ≥ 0.9979). The estimated modulus is highest for steel (199.06 GPa), followed by titanium (116.56 GPa) and aluminum (69.38 GPa). These are pooled estimates; specimen-to-specimen scatter and the limited strain interval should be considered when interpreting them.

![Stress–strain measurements with linear fits](stress_strain_fits.png)

item.text:
The analysis is saved in [results.md](/private/tmp/tmptr0j5t64/pete/projects/elastic-modulus/results.md), with the figure at [stress_strain_fits.png](/private/tmp/tmptr0j5t64/pete/projects/elastic-modulus/stress_strain_fits.png).

The pooled linear fits estimate elastic moduli of **69.38 GPa for aluminum**, **199.06 GPa for steel**, and **116.56 GPa for titanium**. Each fit has R² ≥ 0.9979.
